q: Does the ISAba1-internal promoter posited by Harmer et al. actually drive constitutive marA expression in MRSN 56 in vivo, or is 'ISAba1 next to a MarR-family regulator + frameshifted MarR pseudogene' merely a structural prerequisite that has not yet been shown to produce the transcriptional phenotype?
basis: The paper's headline novel mechanism (IS-mediated marR inactivation with constitutive marA expression from an ISAba1-internal promoter) is asserted from genome architecture. Neither the paper (no RNAseq/qPCR shown for MRSN 56 specifically) nor this replication (no RNAseq run) provides direct transcriptional evidence. The half of the two-step mechanism that is genuinely novel is exactly the half currently unsupported.
next_steps: Obtain a viable MRSN 56 or reconstructed isogenic derivative; run RNAseq +/- ciprofloxacin/norfloxacin challenge; compare marA transcript levels to a marR-restored (repaired) isogenic strain and to a susceptible GC1 reference; map 5' TSSs by rend-seq or 5' RACE to prove the ISAba1-internal promoter is the one being used; couple with a marA ChIP-seq or reporter assay to confirm downstream regulon activation.

q: Which specific MarR-family locus in MRSN 56 is functionally responsible for the derepression phenotype -- the chr 2,317k ISAba1-adjacent intact MarR regulator, the chr 1,422k frameshifted MarR pseudogene, or both acting in combination?
basis: PGAP identifies at least two MarR-family loci with different insults (one adjacent to ISAba1 but structurally intact, one frameshifted pseudogene without an obvious insertion event). The paper collapses this to a single 'marR' story. Distinguishing them experimentally is a non-trivial and unresolved genetic question that matters for translating the mechanism to other genomes.
next_steps: In a susceptible GC1 background, construct clean knockouts of each candidate MarR-family gene individually and jointly; complement each with an intact copy under its native promoter; measure fluoroquinolone MIC and marA/efflux-pump expression in every combination; identify the single locus whose restoration suppresses the phenotype -- if any single locus does. Include a strain in which ISAba1 is precisely reinserted upstream of the intact MarR regulator to test whether the insertion, and not the pseudogene, is the causal event.

q: Is the Tn7+ configuration (canonical Tn7 at attTn7 downstream of glmS fused with an adjacent AbGRI1-derived tetA(B)/sul2 segment) unique to MRSN 56, or has it disseminated across other GC1 or XDR A. baumannii genomes -- and if so, along what phylogenetic path?
basis: The paper reports Tn7+ as a novel structural event but does not survey other genomes for its presence. This replication confirmed the configuration in MRSN 56 but did not probe generality. A novel MGE that has jumped is a very different clinical story from a one-off recombinant.
next_steps: Extract the diagnostic Tn7+ junction sequences (glmS--TnsA and tet(B)--sul2--ISAba1 boundaries, plus the internal 22.85 kb AbGRI1-derived segment); run a structural-variant / junction scan (nucmer, minimap2 with paftools call, or a BLAST-based junction detector) across the ~16,000 A. baumannii genomes in RefSeq and against the SRA/ENA raw-read corpus (using SEARCH or Sourmash); cluster hits by core-genome MLST or wgSNP and infer whether Tn7+ has moved horizontally (independent acquisitions) or spread by lineage descent; time-calibrate to see whether it predates or postdates the MRSN 56 isolation date.

q: How reproducible is the paper's finished MinION+MiSeq Unicycler assembly at the finished (closed chromosome + 4 plasmids) level, and are the paper's exact plasmid boundaries, the two Tn7 copies, and the Tn7+ boundary structure stable across independent modern hybrid assemblers?
basis: This replication starts from the finished GCA_021484925.1 assembly the authors submitted. Every downstream claim depends on that assembly being correct at the base-pair level; we did not re-assemble the raw reads. Modern hybrid assemblers (Trycycler, Flye+medaka+polypolish, hybracter) frequently differ from a 2022 Unicycler v0.4.0 build at repeat resolution -- exactly where Tn7 copies and IS-flanked insertions live.
next_steps: Pull raw reads from ENA/SRA (BioProject PRJNA742487, BioSample SAMN20178847); re-run Unicycler v0.4.0 exactly and modern alternatives (Trycycler consensus of Flye + Raven + miniasm-minipolish followed by polypolish with the Illumina reads; hybracter); compare finished contigs at base-pair resolution against CP090606.1 + CP080453..456 with dnadiff/nucmer; specifically check (a) do all four small plasmids close independently, (b) are the two Tn7 copies each recovered as separate contigs or is one collapsed, (c) is the Tn7+ right-boundary IS element resolved consistently, and (d) does the 22,852 vs 21,700 bp Tn7+ span discrepancy trace to an assembly-boundary ambiguity.

q: What are the fitness costs, MIC ceiling, and clinical stability of the ISAba1->marR->constitutive-marA route to fluoroquinolone resistance compared with the classical gyrA+parC double-mutant route -- and does the novel route make an XDR clone more likely to persist in the hospital environment?
basis: The paper posits a novel FQR route but does not compare its stability or fitness cost to the well-characterized gyrA+parC pathway. Notably, this replication independently flagged parC as a frameshifted pseudogene in MRSN 56 (bonus finding), meaning MRSN 56 in fact carries both routes -- making it impossible from the paper alone to attribute the phenotype's persistence to the novel route specifically.
next_steps: In a common susceptible GC1 background, construct isogenic strains carrying (a) WT, (b) gyrA S83L only, (c) parC pseudogene only, (d) ISAba1->marR inactivation only, (e) all pairwise combinations, (f) the triple; measure FQ MIC (ciprofloxacin, moxifloxacin, levofloxacin), efflux-pump expression, growth rate, competitive-fitness index against WT in mixed culture, and reversion rate over 100 generations of serial passage +/- sub-MIC FQ pressure; ask (i) whether the ISAba1-route strains bear a lower fitness cost than the gyrA/parC-route strains, (ii) whether they revert more slowly, and (iii) whether they achieve the same MIC ceiling. This directly addresses whether the novel route explains the clinical persistence of XDR GC1 lineages.
